text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis B infection with fulminant hepatic failure.

The combination of recent high-risk sexual behavior, acute onset of jaundice, agitation (likely hepatic encephalopathy), and lack of significant alcohol or drug-induced liver injury history strongly points to an acute viral etiology, specifically Hepatitis B.
